label: Morning Brief
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary. This morning's overnight news and filings snapshot was not available for this run, so coverage runs through about 10:40 PM ET on Nov 24.

driver.text: Per Bloomberg's markets wrap, stocks extended their decline and futures signaled further weakness as doubts over the durability of the AI boom drove a retreat from technology shares, while Treasuries advanced on haven demand (5:09 PM ET). Bloomberg also reported the US is set to announce plans to raise tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies, according to people familiar with the matter (6:41 PM ET). In Asia, Bloomberg reported enthusiasm over Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia quickly evaporated as Taiwan stocks tumbled and investors refocused on worries around the global AI trade (9:45 PM ET); the Financial Times said tech stocks in Tokyo and Seoul suffered as the Wall Street bounce faded (8:41 PM ET). Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Alibaba in talks for potential offshore bond sale next year
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Alibaba has been in discussions in recent weeks with banks about potentially raising money in the offshore bond markets next year, according to people familiar with the matter. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.summary: Per WSJ, as Nvidia's co-founder resumes control, the company is working to convince the market it is business as usual while facing fresh challenges. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: UP Fintech logs record near-US$1 billion net asset inflow in Hong Kong
items.summary: Per the South China Morning Post, UP Fintech, parent of Tiger Brokers, said its net asset inflows in Hong Kong approached US$1 billion in the third quarter, the highest since it entered the market. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
